about.description.text: Who builds SAIPEN and why, the multi-agent workflow behind it, the builder principles, and the engineering contract this website holds itself to.

about.motto.body.text: Built by one human working with replaceable AI agents. The agents change. The project state survives.

about.author.body1.text: SAIPEN is created and maintained by [vacterro]({author}) and developed through practical multi-agent workflows: AI coding agents from different vendors do much of the implementation, and a human operator sets direction, decides, audits and keeps the work continuous across them. The protocol is the written-down form of that arrangement.

about.author.body2.text: [SAIPEN HQ]({organization}) is the organization identity, and the [SAIPEN Community]({community}) on Discord is the shared discussion space.

about.why.body1.text: One person running many projects with many agents hits the same wall every day. A session ends, a context limit is reached, a provider has a bad hour, a cheaper model takes over for the afternoon — and every new agent arrives as a brilliant stranger who has to be briefed from scratch: what are we building, what was already tried, what must not be touched, is this actually finished.

about.why.body2.text: The person ends up carrying the project between sessions in their own head, retelling it again and again. That is the failure SAIPEN removes:

about.why.quote.text: The human should not be the project's memory bus.

about.why.body3.text: So the memory moved out of the chat and into the project, in plain files, with one exact next step and rules that make a cold agent continue instead of asking. Everything else in the protocol — checkpoints, VERIFY, evidence, honest WAITs — exists to make that handoff safe.

about.workflow.idea.text: **Idea** — a real problem from running projects, not a hypothetical agent stack.

about.workflow.target.text: **Narrow target** — one ticket with a verify contract, small enough to prove.

about.workflow.agent.text: **Agent** — whichever model and host is available and suited.

about.workflow.verify.text: **VERIFY** — the strongest available check, with a red control first.

about.workflow.audit.text: **Audit** — an independent review, often by a different model, packaged as evidence.

about.workflow.handoff.text: **Handoff** — the session ends; the state is already on disk.

about.workflow.next.text: **Another agent** — runs `saipen continue` and picks up the next step.

about.workflow.tools.text: The operator tooling in the ecosystem grew out of the same loop: {tools}. The longer version is in the design note [How SAIPEN is built: one operator, many agents](/blog/how-saipen-is-built/).
about.workflow.tools.note: {tools} is a list of linked project names built by the page; keep it where the list reads naturally.

about.workflow.and.note: Joins the last two project names in a list, with surrounding spaces.

about.workflow.comma.note: Joins project names in a list.

about.principles.note.text: These are the author's product instincts across SAIPEN and the tools around it — a fingerprint, not protocol law. The normative rules are in the [specification](/spec/).

about.principles.local-first.line.text: State and tools live on your machine. A hosted service is an option, never a requirement.

about.principles.no-account.line.text: Nothing here asks who you are, because nothing here needs to know.

about.principles.open-core.line.text: The protocol, its specification and its validator are public and MIT-licensed.

about.principles.independence.line.text: Any agent that can read files can continue the work; no vendor owns the memory.

about.principles.visible-state.line.text: Markdown, JSON and logs a person can open in a text editor, diff and commit.

about.principles.evidence.line.text: A check proves it can fail before it is trusted; "done" needs a recorded result.

about.principles.degrade.name.text: Degrade gracefully where it is safe

about.principles.degrade.line.text: Missing capabilities lower the mode explicitly instead of failing silently or pretending.

about.principles.automate.line.text: If a human has to repeat the same briefing or click twice a day, it is a tool waiting to be written.

about.principles.control.line.text: Direction, destructive steps and publication are human decisions — but no one should have to babysit every continuation.

about.dogfooding.title.text: This website is built under SAIPEN

about.dogfooding.body.text: The site you are reading is itself a SAIPEN project, built by AI agents working through the same lifecycle the docs describe. The list below is read at build time from this repository's own `.saipen/BOARD.md`, not typed by hand.

about.dogfooding.red.text: Every gate below was shown able to fail before its green result was trusted:

about.dogfooding.none.text: This build was made from a checkout without project memory, so there is nothing to show.

about.scope.body.text: The public surface of the SAIPEN protocol: documentation, a generated specification reference, the ecosystem catalogue and a deterministic playground. It explains and indexes; it does not define.

about.scope.not-protocol.text: **Not the protocol.** The protocol is the [SAIPEN repository]({repository}).

about.scope.not-engine.text: **Not an execution engine.** It cannot run an agent and has no backend to run one on.

about.scope.authority.text: **Authority runs one way.** Canonical protocol source outranks the generated reference, which outranks the explanatory docs, which outrank any summary copy. Summary copy never redefines behaviour.

about.beyond.body.text: The protocol does not exist in a vacuum. The author builds local-first tools for AI agents, automation and Windows — AI-agent infrastructure, operator workbenches and quota monitors, desktop utilities, and creative and technical software. Only the projects that belong to SAIPEN are catalogued on the [ecosystem page](/ecosystem/); the rest are on [github.com/vacterro]({author}).

about.design.body.text: The site is a native [Wintage](/ecosystem/#wintage) interface: Golden Default palette, 2px bevels, zero radius, zero shadow, instant interaction — the same design language SAIPEN's own UI.md prescribes for every SAIPEN tool. Text is drawn with pixel-grid faces built from openly licensed fonts, so it renders without anti-aliasing. The [design note](/blog/no-antialiasing-on-the-web/) explains how and how it is tested.

about.a11y.landmarks.text: A skip link, one `main`, labelled navigation landmarks and one `h1` per page, with no skipped heading levels.

about.a11y.focus.text: Visible, hard-edged focus on every control; the theme menu is a labelled native select.

about.a11y.nojs.text: Navigation and disclosures are native elements and work with JavaScript disabled.

about.a11y.colour.text: No state is carried by colour alone: every badge and callout has a word.

about.a11y.text.text: Text is real DOM text: selectable, searchable, translatable and readable by screen readers.

about.a11y.motion.text: No motion except the one-pixel press of a button; reduced-motion preferences are respected.

about.perf.body.text: Mostly static HTML with small scripts. `npm run audit:build` fails the build when a page exceeds its HTML budget, when total JavaScript or font weight passes its ceiling, or when a page loads a script it does not need. There is no client framework and no hydration; the twelve pixel faces are 6–17 KB each, and the audit fails if any exceeds 20 KB or all of them together exceed 200 KB.

about.gates.build.text: Static production build; content front-matter is schema-validated here.

about.gates.lint.text: Style law: no radius, shadow, blur, transparency, motion, hex colour, em unit or size without its pixel face.

about.gates.validate-themes.text: All 16 palettes carry exactly the 21 tokens.

about.gates.validate-canonical.text: The protocol snapshot still matches its recorded SHA-256 hashes.

about.gates.validate-content.text: Every internal link and anchor in the built site resolves; no duplicate ids; required metadata present.

about.gates.validate-baselines.text: Every versioned screenshot baseline is present and matches the manifest, so an archive cannot silently drop the visual evidence.

about.gates.audit-build.text: Structure, theme contract, route registry, performance budget and protocol data of the built output.

about.gates.test-pixel.text: Every pixel of every page is one of the palette colours, in Chromium and WebKit.

about.gates.test-shell.text: Routes, maturity badges, navigation, breadcrumbs, landmarks, overflow at 320 / 390 / 640 / 1280 px.

about.gates.test-content.text: Docs chrome, spec visualizer and aliases, playground, search, agent-readable files.

about.gates.test-runtime.text: Theme persistence, pre-paint restore, fallback and nested palette isolation.

about.gates.test-visual.text: Screenshot baselines, compared with zero tolerance.

about.deploy.static.text: Fully static output with directory-style URLs and a trailing slash on every page.

about.deploy.links.text: Every internal link is root-relative; the canonical origin ({domain}) is configured in one place.

about.deploy.generated.text: A [404 page](/404.html), [sitemap.xml](/sitemap.xml), [robots.txt](/robots.txt) and [llms.txt](/llms.txt) are generated with the build.

about.deploy.aliases.text: Aliases such as `/spec/latest/` are static redirects that need no server rules.

about.deploy.status.text: The site is not deployed: attaching a domain and a host is future gate FG-001. Everything it ships is redistributable — the pixel faces come from DejaVu Sans and Spleen with their licence notices, checked by `npm run validate:licenses`, and listed with the other shipped assets in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.
